launch-or-portland-washington-park.summary: Portland's 410-acre west-hills destination with the Oregon Zoo, rose and Japanese gardens, Hoyt Arboretum, museums, memorials, playground, trails, viewpoints, MAX service, and a free internal shuttle.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.hours: The outdoor park is open 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and closes to vehicles at 10:00 p.m.; every garden, zoo, museum, visitor center, shuttle, and concession keeps its own schedule.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.parking: Parking is limited and pay-by-plate daily 9:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m., normally $2.40 per hour up to $9.60, with higher event rates possible. Route to the exact attraction lot rather than one park pin.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.arrival: MAX Red and Blue lines stop at Washington Park Station near the zoo. A free seasonal shuttle links major attractions and is usually easier than moving a car between full lots.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available at major developed destinations, including park attractions and selected trail nodes, but hours vary and wooded routes do not have continuous facilities.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.cost: The park, Rose Test Garden, memorials, playground, arboretum trails, and shuttle are free. Zoo, Japanese Garden, World Forestry Center exhibits, parking, food, and programs charge separately.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.accessibility: The park lists accessible play, restrooms, parking, and paved routes; MAX and the seasonal shuttle are accessible. Hills, stairs, natural trails, and attraction entrances vary substantially.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary park areas and trails under posted rules, but the zoo, Japanese Garden, playground, buildings, gardens, and events have separate restrictions.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.family: The zoo, playground, arboretum, rose garden, memorial walks, and shuttle create many family options. Plan one or two zones rather than trying to walk the entire hilly park.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.transit: MAX is the most dependable car-free arrival. TriMet buses, biking, walking, rideshare, the seasonal park shuttle, and the 2026 Forest and Washington Park Express add options.
launch-or-portland-washington-park.need: Warm weekends create heavy congestion. Check attraction hours, shuttle season, weather closures, reservoir construction, and event parking before leaving; never assume the park's hours apply to a ticketed attraction.

launch-or-portland-forest-park.summary: A 5,200-acre urban forest with more than 80 trail miles, over 40 access points, the 30-mile Wildwood Trail, Leif Erikson Drive, Balch Creek, Stone House, and connections toward Pittock Mansion and Washington Park.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.hours: The natural area is open 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Trail hazards, storms, landslides, fallen trees, fire conditions, and maintenance can close individual access points at any time.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.parking: Parking is free but highly variable: many trailheads have ten or fewer spaces, while Lower Macleay, Pittock/Wildwood, Lower Saltzman, and Germantown have larger areas. Never block neighbors or road shoulders.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.arrival: Choose a named trailhead and route before traveling; Forest Park is too large for a single useful arrival point. Lower Macleay is the simplest start for Balch Creek and Stone House.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.restrooms: Facilities are limited and concentrated at a few developed trailheads or adjacent destinations. Carry water and do not assume a restroom or fountain will be open at a rustic access point.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.cost: Trails and parking are free. Pittock Mansion admission, guided programs, transportation, equipment, food, and nearby attractions cost separately.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.accessibility: ADA parking exists at Lower Macleay and Wildwood/Pittock trailheads. Trail surface, grade, roots, mud, bridges, and washouts vary; use the official pocket guide for accessible-route details.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed everywhere. Off-leash dogs, fires, drones, camping, fireworks, hunting, fishing, and motorized vehicles are prohibited.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.family: Lower Macleay to Stone House can work for trail-ready families, while the full Wildwood Trail is a serious undertaking. Expect mud, roots, cyclists or horses on designated routes, and few facilities.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.transit: TriMet lines 26, 15, and 77 reach Lower Macleay-area access; Line 16 serves northern trailheads. The free summer 2026 Express Shuttle also serves selected Forest Park stops.
launch-or-portland-forest-park.need: Download the map before entering and check Portland's Trail Closures and Delays page. The Ridge Trail parking area is closed indefinitely and the Wildwood bridge at mile 15.2 has a stepped bypass.

launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.address: Naito Parkway between S Harrison Street and NW Glisan Street, Portland, OR 97204
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.summary: Downtown Portland's 30-acre Willamette riverfront spine with paved greenway, fountains, plazas, public art, memorials, docks, lawns, festival grounds, bridges, Saturday Market access, and skyline views.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-midnight. Interactive fountains, docks, restrooms, markets, festivals, construction zones, and temporary event enclosures use separate hours.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.parking: Use downtown garages, metered streets, transit, biking, walking, or rideshare. Major festivals and races close streets and remove ordinary curb access; do not expect park-side parking.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.arrival: The park stretches more than a mile. Route to the Japanese American Historical Plaza in the north, Salmon Street Springs near the center, or the Bowl and marina area in the south.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.restrooms: An accessible restroom is listed, and temporary facilities appear during major events. Availability is not continuous along the entire waterfront, so identify the nearest open facility before walking far.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.cost: Ordinary park access, paths, lawns, memorials, and fountains are free. Parking, food, market purchases, cruises, rentals, and ticketed or fenced events cost separately.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.accessibility: The riverfront has long paved, generally level routes, accessible transit, and an accessible restroom, though bridge approaches, crowds, event fencing, and construction can change circulation.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed throughout the park. Keep pets away from interactive fountain jets, food areas, crowded events, docks, and posted restricted spaces.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.family: Fountains, river views, boats, bridges, markets, lawns, and festivals can make an easy downtown family outing. Supervise closely beside water, bikes, traffic crossings, and crowded events.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.transit: MAX, buses, Portland Streetcar, Biketown, walking routes, and bridge paths serve different sections. Transit is usually more reliable than driving during waterfront events.
launch-or-portland-tom-mccall-waterfront.need: Event calendars matter here more than at most parks. Waterfront Blues Festival, Rose Festival, races, demonstrations, Saturday Market, construction, and fountain maintenance can transform access from one day to the next.

launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.address: SE 60th Avenue and Salmon Street, Portland, OR 97215
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.summary: A 176-acre park on an extinct volcanic cinder cone with summit views, forest trails, historic open reservoirs, playground, courts, amphitheater, dog area, picnics, community garden, and Portland's annual adult soapbox derby.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-11:59 p.m.; vehicle access is 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Roads close to motor vehicles all day Wednesday and from 10:00 p.m.-5:00 a.m. otherwise.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.parking: Lots and street parking serve different elevations. A summit lot has one designated van space, but Wednesdays require walking or rolling uphill from an open perimeter entrance.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.arrival: Use SE 60th and Salmon for the main vehicle approach, then choose summit, reservoir, playground, amphitheater, dog area, or garden before parking. Internal roads and stairs create substantial elevation changes.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.restrooms: An accessible restroom is available at the summit, with additional seasonal or event facilities possible. Do not assume every picnic, trail, reservoir, or playground zone has a nearby open restroom.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.cost: General park access, trails, viewpoints, playground, courts, and ordinary picnics are free. Reservations, programs, concessions, and special events may charge.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.accessibility: The park lists accessible picnic, play, and summit-restroom facilities. The paved route to play has a moderate slope, while forest trails, stairs, and the summit climb vary greatly.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.dogs: A designated off-leash area is available; dogs must be leashed elsewhere and are prohibited inside the amphitheater on concert days.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.family: The playground, reservoirs, summit views, lawns, picnics, and short trails suit many ages, but steep grades and traffic on vehicle-open days require planning.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.transit: Bus, biking, walking, rideshare, and driving reach the surrounding neighborhood. Expect an uphill walk from transit or perimeter streets and verify current route service.
launch-or-portland-mt-tabor-park.need: The picnic shelter is being rebuilt May-August 2026, closing the shelter site and two nearby paths. Wednesdays are car-free, and events such as the PDX Adult Soapbox Derby can close roads and fill the park.

launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.address: NW corner of SE Cesar E. Chavez Boulevard and Stark Street, Portland, OR 97214
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.summary: A 32-acre historic Olmsted-style neighborhood destination with Firwood Lake, mature trees, accessible playground, picnic grove, paved and natural paths, courts, lawns, public art, and a scheduled dog off-leash area.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-10:30 p.m. Off-leash hours change by season, weekday, and weekend; reservations and volunteer events use separate schedules.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.parking: Street parking surrounds the park; there is no large destination lot. Use the exact edge nearest the playground, picnic grove, courts, dog area, or lake and respect residential driveways.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.arrival: The park has distinct north, south, lake, play, sport, and dog-use zones. The official map is useful because paths curve through dense mature landscaping rather than following a simple grid.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.restrooms: An accessible restroom is listed, along with accessible picnic facilities. Confirm location and seasonal availability before relying on it for a group visit.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.cost: General park, playground, paths, lake views, courts, and ordinary use are free. Reserved picnics, organized events, transportation, and external services may cost.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.accessibility: A paved path reaches the play area, which includes a ramp, transfer station, sensory play, and adapted high-back swing. Accessible restroom and picnic tables are listed.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.dogs: Off-leash use is limited to the designated area and official seasonal time windows; dogs must be leashed elsewhere and kept out of the playground and sensitive pond edge.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.family: The accessible playground, lawns, ducks and turtles, paths, picnic shade, and courts work well for families. Firwood Lake is for viewing, not swimming or wading.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.transit: Frequent eastside buses, biking, walking, rideshare, and street parking reach surrounding blocks. Select the edge closest to your activity to reduce unnecessary walking.
launch-or-portland-laurelhurst-park.need: Dog off-leash hours are easy to misunderstand and change seasonally. Duckweed on Firwood Lake is a monitored native plant condition, not a swimming invitation; keep children and pets out of the water.

launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.address: N Edison Street and Pittsburg Avenue, Portland, OR 97203
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.summary: A 22-acre Willamette riverfront park beneath the Gothic arches of St. Johns Bridge with a nature patch, amphitheater, lawns, paths, dock, boat ramp, beach access, dog area, public art, and one of Portland's defining views.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-midnight. Boat-ramp parking, docks, events, construction, and off-leash use have separate posted conditions; no overnight parking or moorage is allowed.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.parking: Small free lots serve the boat ramp and dog area; the trailer lot is pay-to-park at $5 per day, generally 5:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Spaces are limited during boating and events.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.arrival: Use N Baltimore and N Bradford for flatter riverfront paths, or arrive from upper St. Johns for bridge stairs, nature patch, and overlooks. The park has steep and flat zones.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.restrooms: An accessible restroom is listed. Boaters and event visitors should confirm current opening and temporary-facility arrangements before depending on it.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.cost: General park, bridge views, paths, nature patch, beach edge, and ordinary dock access are free. Trailer parking, permits, events, rentals, and transportation may cost.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.accessibility: Flat paved paths are available from the lower parking area, but upper approaches and bridge stairs are steep. The park lists an accessible restroom and developed waterfront routes.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.dogs: A designated off-leash area is available; leash dogs elsewhere and keep them under control near boats, beach wildlife, events, and the river.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.family: Bridge views, lawns, nature patch, boats, shore exploration, and paths can suit families. The beach and dock are unsupervised river access, not a lifeguarded swimming facility.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.transit: TriMet serves St. Johns, with walking or rolling required down to the riverfront. Biking, rideshare, driving, and bridge walking are options, but grades are significant.
launch-or-portland-cathedral-park.need: St. Johns Bridge repairs and Bradford Street environmental cleanup work can affect specific areas. State agencies currently do not recommend altering park activities, but obey fencing and check project updates before visiting.

launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.address: 700 N Rosa Parks Way, Portland, OR 97217
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.summary: A formal 16-acre City Beautiful park with Portland's first public rose garden, historic bandstand and community center, second-oldest playground, seasonal outdoor pool, splash pad, sports courts, fields, picnic facilities, and paved paths.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-midnight; tennis lights turn off at 10:00 p.m. The community center, outdoor pool, splash pad, rose-garden services, and reservations keep seasonal schedules.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.parking: Use street parking around N Rosa Parks Way and surrounding blocks. Route to the rose garden, pool, community center, playground, courts, or field before choosing an edge.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.arrival: The formal rose garden and fountain anchor the center, with community center, pool, playground, courts, and fields around it. The park is compact enough to walk but each facility has a distinct entrance.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.restrooms: An accessible restroom is listed, with additional facilities inside the community center and pool only during their operating hours.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.cost: The park, rose garden, playground, splash pad when operating, paths, and most courts are free. Pool admission, classes, reservations, and programs may charge.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.accessibility: The park lists accessible picnic and restroom facilities and mostly paved formal paths. Pool, community center, playground equipment, and historic structures have facility-specific access details.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed throughout the park and are not allowed in the rose beds, splash pad, pool, playground, or indoor facilities except as permitted by law.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.family: Playground, seasonal pool, splash pad, rose garden, fountain, lawns, and sports make this one of North Portland's most varied family parks.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.transit: Bus routes, biking, walking, rideshare, and neighborhood street parking serve N Rosa Parks Way. Verify current TriMet arrivals and pool schedules before a time-sensitive trip.
launch-or-portland-peninsula-park.need: Do not confuse the decorative rose-garden fountain with the seasonal splash pad. Water play and pool operations are seasonal and can close for maintenance, staffing, weather, or water-quality checks.

launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.summary: A 600-acre extinct cinder cone with meadow and forest trails, broad Cascade views, wildlife habitat, visitor center, accessible restroom, and designated hiking, mountain-biking, and equestrian routes.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.hours: The park is open 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Main road and lot hours are seasonal: generally 7:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter, 8:00 p.m. in spring and fall, and 10:00 p.m. in summer.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.parking: The main visitor-center lot is reached from SE 162nd Avenue and closes promptly at the seasonal gate time. Secondary neighborhood trailheads have limited street access and different facilities.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.arrival: For a first visit, use the main entrance and visitor center, then choose summit meadow or a named trail. Return to the lot well before the gate closes; park hours do not guarantee vehicle access.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.restrooms: An accessible restroom is listed at the visitor-center area. Remote trails and neighborhood entrances do not provide dependable facilities or water.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.cost: Park, trails, visitor-center access, views, and parking are free. Programs, transportation, equipment, and external services may cost.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.accessibility: The visitor-center area includes an accessible restroom and developed routes, but trail grade and surface vary. Use the official map to select a route appropriate for mobility needs.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.dogs: Dogs are allowed only while leashed and on trail; off-leash and off-trail use are prohibited to protect wildlife and habitat.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.family: The visitor center, summit meadow, views, wildlife, and selectable trail lengths can suit prepared families. There is no playground, and exposed meadow weather changes quickly.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.transit: Bus, biking, rideshare, and driving serve the SE Powell area, but the main visitor center sits uphill from the arterial. Confirm the complete walking route before using transit.
launch-or-portland-powell-butte-nature-p.need: The main entrance may close during freezing or icy conditions, and its gate closes promptly at seasonal times. Check weather, smoke, wind, trail conditions, and sunset before committing to a long loop.
